locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_quantitative_rmt_round14.md · A quantitative finite witness for every fixed rank
statement: For the formal fixed-rank cosine series M and a real zero 0<t_*≤1/d, let R=2/d and B≥1 majorize |M| on |z|=R. With L=ceil(log_2(8B(B+1))), the two degree-L Taylor polynomials of exp(±t_*x/2) give a strictly negative two-by-two moment determinant. The order-L Hankel form is therefore not positive semidefinite, using moments through degree 2L. A sufficient explicit majorant is B=J! D^J exp((J−1)HR+HR²/4), D=(2J−1)16^(2J−2)(2J−1)! exp(1+R d exp(b)).
hypotheses: Fixed positive integer rank J and 0<a<b<1, H=log(b/a), d=b−a. The form is for the extrapolated cosine series. The bound is sufficient, not generally the least witness order.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_quantitative_rmt_round14.md · At rank one the least order is known exactly
statement: At rank one set σ²=H/2. The order-L formal Hankel form is congruent to I−(d/σ²)T_L, with Hermite Jacobi edges σ sqrt(k), 1≤k≤L. A negative witness exists exactly when the largest zero of He_(L+1) strictly exceeds σ/d. Equality gives singular positive semidefiniteness. The least order lies above σ²/(4d²) and at most floor(σ²/d²)+1; it is σ²/(4d²)+O(σ/d) as σ/d→infinity.
hypotheses: Fixed positive band at rank one, with the formal Gaussian density modifier 1−d x/σ². He denotes the probabilists' Hermite polynomial. The asymptotic concerns small d/σ, and the criterion does not test the true law outside the supported moment window.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_quantitative_rmt_round14.md · At rank one the least order is known exactly
statement: For the standardized series exp(z²/2)(1−z/2), all principal minors through Hankel order two are nonnegative and q(x)=2x³+9x²+6x−3 has formal square expectation −30. At standardized tilt 1/sqrt(3), after rescaling y=sqrt(3)x, the order-two form is singular positive semidefinite, y²+3y is null, and y³+4y²+12y has square expectation −27.
hypotheses: Exact rational formal-moment fixtures with director replay. They check the strict Hermite threshold and are separate from the general degree proof.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_quantitative_rmt_round14.md · The exact Petrov tail quotient has a positive finite representation
statement: With L=P_nT(φ_+)|P_n, M=U*L^(−*)L^(−1)U and A_n=P_nT(φ)|P_n, the tilted-to-ambient Fredholm ratio is det S, S=M^(−1/2)(U*A_n^(−1)U)M^(−1/2), and det Γ(z)/det Γ(0)=det M. For real z the ratio is in [exp(−H_N z²/4),1]; det M and det(U*A_n^(−1)U) lie in [exp(−J|z|H_N),exp(J|z|H_N)]. The mass-removed complementary determinant has liminf at least exp(−2JH z_*) at any positive formal zero z_*.
hypotheses: Fixed N≥2 and deleted rank J≥1, n=N+J−1, global rooted cosine CUE model, real z, fixed positive band for uniformity in N. No invertibility of Petrov's optional fixed-tail chart is needed.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_quantitative_rmt_round14.md · A true-cutoff continuum Gram and a factorial approximation
statement: For real z≥0, e^(−H_N z)M_ij converges to E[1_(max(p,q)≤1) ∫_(max(p,q))^1 u_i(t−p)u_j(t−q)dt], with independent compound-Poisson shift totals p,q of intensity z dx/(2x) on [a,b] and shifted orthonormal Legendre profiles u_j. For p,q≤1 its kernel differs from the transposed oriented formal kernel by an ordinary lower interval of length min(p,q).
hypotheses: Fixed rank and 0<a<b<1. Exact Gram limit with the finite convolution cutoff. Pure-sign agreement is within the coefficient window; the formal extrapolation can use unsupported shifts.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_quantitative_rmt_round14.md · A true-cutoff continuum Gram and a factorial approximation
statement: For h=H(φ_−/φ_+), the Hilbert–Schmidt error after cutting both indices at M_cut≥n is at most |z|sqrt(H_N/2) times ∑_(s≥floor(M_cut/k_*)) (|z|H_N)^s/s!, where k_* is the maximum band index. Schatten Hölder bounds the induced trace-norm K error, and the log-determinant quotient error is at most twice that error divided by exp(−2|z|H_N).
hypotheses: Fixed positive band, fixed deleted rank, real z in a compact interval. A nonempty finite band is required for k_*; an empty band has K=0 and both tails equal one.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_arithmetic_strata_round14.md · Exact effective modulus and removal of several strata
statement: For fixed Mangoldt factor ν, put g=(k,ν), q=k/g, M=kT/ν and δ=H/T. The centered divisor twist reduces exactly to a unit numerator at q and vanishes when q=1. It is bounded by O_B(M log(2+M)(1+Hg/√(kTν))^(−B)) and O_B(q δ^(−2)(q²/(Mδ²))^B). Thus ν/g²≤(H²/(kT))T^(−δ_0) can be discarded with arbitrary fixed-power savings for a fixed positive margin δ_0.
hypotheses: Compact comparable-height cutoff with derivative bounds, T≈Y, k≤Y^θ, H=T^κ and fixed κ>(1+θ)/2 for the short-factor claim. The weak pointwise loss O_ε(qT^ε) requires choosing κ close to one and then a small positive B. The divisor argument n need not be coprime to q.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_arithmetic_strata_round14.md · Exact effective modulus and removal of several strata
statement: All supported prime powers sharing a prime with the modulus contribute o(T). All powers p^j with j≥3 contribute O(Y^θ T^(1/3+ε) log^C T), hence o(T) for θ<2/3 with fixed power margin and sufficiently small ε.
hypotheses: The fixed d₂*(Λ log²) smooth signed sum, four-prime-supported bounded outer coefficients c_k, T≈Y, fixed 0<a<b, θ=4b∈(1/2,2/3). The taper exponent is chosen sufficiently near one. This is an unconditional estimate for these arithmetic strata.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_arithmetic_strata_round14.md · Ghosh's primary quadratic estimate removes every square in a strict range
statement: At k≈K and square base p≈X the reduced quadratic numerator estimate, weighted over gcd classes, costs O(T^ε(KT/X)[K^(−1/4)+X^(−1/8)+K^(1/4)X^(−1/2)]). Combined with small-X pointwise control it gives a power saving for all square factors when 1/2<θ<9/17, equivalently 1/8<b<9/68.
hypotheses: Same compact signed sum and bounded four-prime coefficients. Ghosh's thesis Theorem 2 on exact reduced rational phases, two monotone taper transitions and fixed strict power margins. The endpoint and the genuine-prime stratum are outside this estimate.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_arithmetic_strata_round14.md · Divisor Voronoi and averaged inverse-prime bounds
statement: For K≈T^θ and P≈T^ξ, the coprime genuine-prime block saves a power in either open region: Baker θ/2<ξ<θ, (11/10)θ+(4/5)ξ<1 and θ+(11/12)ξ<1; Fouvry–Shparlinski 0<ξ<(3/2)θ, (13/10)θ+(3/5)ξ<1 and (13/12)θ+(5/6)ξ<1. Centered divisor Voronoi and a uniform O(T^ε δ^(−5/2)) cumulative kernel-and-first-derivative envelope permit full dual gcd resolution.
hypotheses: 1/2<θ<2/3 on the stated dyadic scales. Use averages at common prime endpoints and reduce each nonunit dual index to modulus k/gcd(k,l). No least-prime-factor restriction on these gcd estimates. Choose the taper exponent sufficiently near one on compact subsets of the strict regions. The longer-prime scales remain outside them.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_arithmetic_strata_round14.md · An alternate inverse-prime input and an excluded shortcut
statement: The 2018 homogeneous Korolev unit-numerator prefix estimate and common short dual truncation give a power saving near P=T^(1−θ) on K≈T^θ for 1/2<θ<10/17; the principal inverse-prime exponent at the center is (64+17θ)/74 before the small taper and interval losses.
hypotheses: Original homogeneous theorem range q^(7/10+ε)≤X≤q, fixed strict margins, supported modulus primes above Y^a and common dual truncation below Y^a. Prime partial summation adds one vertical factor and changes the cutoff cost to δ^(−3−2B). The later inhomogeneous theorem with two unit coefficients is a different result.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_arithmetic_strata_round14.md · An alternate inverse-prime input and an excluded shortcut
statement: The character twist of d₂*(Λ log²) is L(s,χ)²(−L'/L)'' in absolute convergence. At a simple zero ρ it has residue −2L'(ρ,χ)²; at a zero of order at least two there is no pole. Hence a contour move treating the full twist as an ordinary divisor/Eisenstein twist would omit these zero residues.
hypotheses: Ordinary Dirichlet characters with their Euler factors. The statement concerns the indicated meromorphic continuation and poles at zeros, not a bound on their residue sum. Freezing the prime factor gives a different, valid divisor transform. No Dirichlet GRH is assumed.
